answers.answer: Yes. Green’s separate ALWAYS Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including Reclaim/gain. It chooses one optional group and also performs the Always placement.

evidence.text: - **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there. A later Build needs a fresh decision and another disk: starting with three, Green may skip the Ravage, retain a two-disk Sacred Site, then skip the Build and end with one disk. **Steady Regeneration**'s Healthy/Blighted test refers to the Blight Card, not Blight in the destination land. When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]

requested_parts: Repeat nightmare destruction Fear from same Town in one Tsunami use
answers.answer: No. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once, even if it is moved and damaged again later in that use.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]

requested_parts: Whether turning unearned Fear Card face-up earns it or resolves it
answers.answer: No. Turning it face-up only previews it; it is neither earned nor resolved. It must still be earned and resolved normally.

evidence.text: - **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Bringer can Remove/Replace, add real Blight (destroying Presence normally), modify Invader actions or cause actual Ravage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** may turn any face-down Fear Card face-up, whether already earned or anywhere in the deck. This only previews the card: turning it face-up neither earns it nor resolves its Fear effect early; normal earning and resolution still apply. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type.
